newsitem.title: USA: Greenspan reiterates need for banking law reform.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan reiterates need for banking law reform.

text.p: Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan on Wednesday reiterated that it was important to abolish the Depression-era laws that separate banking from other financial services.
"The Glass-Steagall Act is one of those anachronisms that the sooner it is repealed, the better," Greenspan told the Senate Banking Committee.

Banking Committee Chairman Alfonse D'Amato, a Republican from New York, concluded the second part of Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony to Congress by concurring with the Fed Chairman that Glass-Steagall reform was important.
"I think it's long overdue," D'Amato said.
